notes.title: 1.0.5 - The 'First Class' Update is here!
notes.content:
Major Update! 
Hey everyone! we’re excited to announce The First Class Update is now live! This major quality-of-life update adds additional polish and some final touches, based on player feedback we've received since launch!

To celebrate, we’re offering our deepest discount yet. From 2nd - 9th June, Loco Motive is 20% off! 
Tell your friends, your heirs, and any sworn adversaries!

There’s never been a better time to play, so climb aboard! You’ll be playing the most refined version of Loco Motive to date, complete with extra polish and optimisations designed to enhance your experience.

You can find a full rundown of the patch notes below, but here's a brief overview:

Update Overview

 Refined puzzle logic, for smoother gameplay across key chapters
 Improvements to UI, such as mouse wheel scrolling in the inventory!
 Numerous bugs squashed, enhancing overall stability and player experience
 Additional polish, to animations, environment visuals, and more!
 English (US) localisation introduced, alongside the existing English (UK) version
 Overhauled Autosave system, improving performance and reliability

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/d08f1cb466e983a35fd85f4dbb6e03f0d1c722dd.png

MCV/Develop Awards 

Great news, folks! We’ve been shortlisted for Visual Innovation of the Year in the upcoming 2025 MCV/DEVELOP Awards, taking place in London, UK on June 19, 2025. 

The MCV/DEVELOP Awards have been around for over 20 years, and aim to recognise the successes of the UK games industry in every area that it excels. We worked on Loco Motive for close to four years, so it’s immensely cool to be recognised by our peers, and to be nominated alongside some incredible titles. Fingers crossed and best of luck to everybody!

You can check out the full shortlist here.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/c3a7ed0caa65576f3ef37f34e2ce0165b61b5c6f.jpg

New Milestone Reached!

We've crunched the numbers and we're so excited to share that Loco Motive has now sold over 30,000 copies across PC and Nintendo Switch. This is a huge milestone for a small team like ours, especially with our debut title. It truly means the world to us. If you played Loco Motive at launch, told a friend about us, or even spread the word on socials, then we couldn’t have reached this point without you! Thank you so much for your continued feedback, passion, and support!

notes.title: The Road Ahead!
notes.content:
Happy New Year! 

After a short post launch break over the holidays, we jumped back into things last week and are now looking towards our next major update for Loco Motive.

1.0.4 was successful in addressing the majority of issues reported by our community after launch, but we still have a few sneaky lingering bugs to investigate. Our first priority will be to fix remaining issues and continue to improve the player experience.

In the new year we were humbled to recieve the Adventure Game Of The Year award from The Adventure Game Hotspot, and to have received six nominations in the upcoming AGOTY Awards, 

We deeply appreciate all of the feedback and support we’ve received so far!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/d509e68c9cbf32c640bb79005ee534cbd8ce8157.png

Quality Of Life Update

Outside of bug squashing, we’re working towards a bigger Quality of Life Update which will take into account the community feedback we’ve received post launch.

This update will include:

 UI fixes
 Minor puzzle enhancements
 New Features
 Reworked Autosave for a better experience with save games. 

That’s not an exhaustive list, but we’ll be sharing more details in an upcoming dev blog!

500!

We’re also fast approaching 500 reviews on Steam! User reviews have been important in helping other players decide whether to play Loco Motive, and we’re very grateful to everyone who has taken the time to leave a review so far!

If you want to chat to us directly about the game, come join our community discussion over on Discord!

notes.title: Patch 1.0.4 is OUT!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We really appreciate your passion and support since the launch—it means a lot to us. Patch 1.0.4 is now live on PC and Nintendo Switch* - This is our first update, and it addresses many of the bugs and issues you've reported since release. 

*(17/12/2024) The patch is now available on Nintendo Switch, thank you for your patience!

Thanks to all of your helpful feedback and reports, we believe we’ve pinpointed the cause of the soft-locking issues. These should now be resolved, and we can’t thank you enough for your patience while we worked on these fixes!

Here’s a rundown of the changes:

[STABILITY]


 fixed soft locks caused by incorrect handling of cancelled interactions
 fixed soft lock that could occur when clicking multiple times on don's broken door
 fixed rare soft lock when interacting with sister Gretchen and brother Jared in chapter two
 fixed soft lock where the band could get stuck in a loop when entering green room in chapter four
 fixed threading issue that could occur when interacting with the band members
 fixed soft lock that could occur when rapidly clicking on the casino patrons
 fixed potential threading issues when showing the perfumed note to characters
 fixed threading issue when talking to the highrollers in the casino
 fixed potential threading issues when leaving dialogue trees
 fixed soft lock due to erroneous character positioning during chapter six
 fixed threading issues when interacting with characters whilst drunk
 fixed a crash on certain windows system languages when looking at the medical records
 fixed null reference exception when an active controller is disconnected due to low battery
 fixed background sequences being stopped when an interaction is cancelled
 fixed soft lock when loading into chapter six from an autosave
 fixed a soft lock when talking to the chefs in chapter three
 fixed threading issues during unhandled fall-back interactions with characters, inventory items & props
 fixed soft lock when giving the briefcase to the twins in chapter two

[DIALOGUE]

 fixed german eszett character not appearing for lines displayed in all caps
 fixed dialogue text rendering off screen when using certain settings
 fixed issue where Lady Unterwald displayed incorrect dialogue options at beginning of chapter four
 fixed subtitle dialogue continuing to show after the twins escape from the vent in chapter four
 fixed accessibility text settings not being applied to background sequence dialogue

[VISUAL]

 fixed doctor Hirsch being very shy and facing the wall during handshake cutscenes in chapter four
 fixed Diana rendering underneath the motorbike in the test yard
 fixed Don remaining invisible if you leave the casino without following him
 fixed visual bug when showing Ron the detective badge at the dining table
 fixed the quartermaster from disappearing when using the hint line in the test yard
 fixed issue where Herman could show the detective badge to characters while in disguise
 fixed visual issues when giving the briefcase to the twins in chapter two
 fixed visual issues when giving the sketches to doctor Hirsch in chapter two
 fixed Philately Stamp visual issues during the mansion lobby cutscene in the finale 
 fixed issue where Don appeared in the post credits cutscene

[GAMEPLAY]

 added specific calls for combining the various knife state items with the slippery mixture
 fixed Arthur not walking towards brother Jared when interacting whilst drunk
 fixed Arthur not walking towards Belle when giving her an item
 fixed suction boots remaining active when using them on the ladder in chapter four
 fixed incendiary pencils remaining active when using them on the firebox in chapter five
 fixed hearing horn background sequence continuing when leaving the room
 fixed Don's betting sequence being triggered if you enter the casino whilst he's leaving for the dining carriage
 fixed Don and Bergmann background sequence continuing when leaving the room
 fixed publisher pigeon background sequence continuing when looking at the in-tray

[SAVES]

 fix for save states affected by erroneous character positioning in chapter six
 fixed handshake club lights issue on initial autosave after Arthur drinks the rosebud
 fixed autosave icon not disappearing if an action was cancelled by the player

[UI]

 updated credits list
 fixed the console being accessible on release builds
 fixed tutorial popups not disappearing if an action was cancelled by the player


We encourage you to keep sharing your feedback and thoughts on forums and social media. We’re actively reading your comments and taking note of areas where we can improve in future updates. If you come across any more issues, please report them! This helps us investigate your specific case and implement fixes more quickly.

Thank you so much for your continued feedback, passion, and support during this time!

notes.title: Thank You For Playing!
notes.content:
To all of you that have picked up Loco Motive at launch, thank you for playing!

In just a few days we became one of the highest rated new releases on Metacritic, and achieved the “Very Positive” rating on Steam! This kind of response really means the world to us! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/7c4b81b39d1f35b6cbd29adf88d2b6126f4836d8.gif

We already picked up some glowing Steam reviews from you at launch:


“A true gem for point and click adventure lovers. From the art style to the story and voice acting, this game had me grinning from ear to ear and giggling at my desk. I am so happy I waited patiently for this! I highly recommend for fans of the genre - you won't be disappointed!” - André Conti

“It's well written (actually funny and high quality writing) and the voice acting is top tier for the genre. The art and animations are stunning. The puzzles are good. It works great with mouse/kbd or a controller (I've played 100% with controller so far and it's a great implementation). The music is just fantastic. This has to be one of the top point and clicks in the last few years.” - GeorgeBroussard

Try Hard Guides - 10/10

"With its beautiful pixel art, great humor, and outstanding voice acting, Loco Motive is a captivating blend of next-gen and yesteryear, taking everything we love about classic point-and-click adventures and giving it a fresh, modern spin."

 Adventure Game Hotspot - 9.5/10

“Loco Motive is the full package. Grab a ticket, put on your thinking cap, and hop on the Reuss Express, as this is one of the finest cartoon point-and-click adventures ever created.”

GameLuster - 9/10

"Loco Motive is a worthy successor to the classic point-and-click pixel adventures, featuring a twisty mystery and a cast of memorable, hilarious characters."

Once we’ve addressed things that need our immediate attention, we will start looking at some further Quality Of Life features, but more on that to come!

notes.title: Development Update #13
notes.content:
🎊Loco Motive is finished!🎊

Let's get straight into it, we've hit our biggest milestone yet! - After several years in development, we're very pleased to confirm that Loco Motive is complete. We'll be continuing to squash any bugs in the lead up to launch, of course, but the work is done. We made an entire video-game, people!

We've had a few questions about whether we are still intending to release Loco Motive in Q4 2024.. 

Yes! we'll be announcing our release date very soon, so please stay tuned for impending updates! 


🎙️Role Call! - Voice Cast Announced🎙️

Earlier last month we gave the green light for our talented voice cast to announce their roles, and they delivered with gusto! Huge thanks to Kimlinh Tran and Kirsty Gilmore for casting! - we're proud to confirm (in Alphabetical order) that Loco Motive features the vocal talents of:

Jack Ayres as Gunter Gudrun, Hagen Gudrun, Jimmy

Jack is a Welsh actor and Voice Actor originally from Cardiff, South Wales. Jack has established himself as a versatile and rising voice actor for video games and character voices having featured in almost 40 video game titles as of 2024, including Baldur’s Gate III and Black Myth: Wukong.

Samantha Béart as April Benelli

Samantha is a BAFTA and DICE nominated, GANG Award-winning actor. In the world of videogames, they are best known for their role as Karlach in Baldur’s Gate III, but you may also know them as Thomasina in the critically acclaimed adventure game “The Excavation of Hob’s Barrow”.

Sally Beaumont as Beverly Moore, Sister Gretchen, Quinn Morgan, Florence Schreiber, Pearl Wexler, Shelly Gedling 

Sally is a voice actor living in Oxford, UK and no stranger to voicing adventure game characters, having played a wide range across 30+ video game titles. This includes The Excavation of Hob's Barrow, a leading role as Fia in the upcoming Old Skies, and a stand out performance as Weeoo in Harold Halibut.

Alasdair Beckett-King as The Handshake Leader

Alasdair is an author, actor, video game writer and award-winning stand-up comedian, winner of the 2017 Leicester Mercury Comedian of the Year, and Chortle's Breakthrough Comedian of the Year in 2023. Alasdair is also the creator of the Nelly Cootalot series of adventure games.

Sean Chiplock as Arthur Ackerman

Sean has been an avid participant in videogame culture ever since his childhood, so it’s no surprise that he enjoys performing for them just as much as he enjoys playing them. In the world of videogames, Sean has featured in everything from AAA behemoths like The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Genshin Impact to indie success stories such as the recent Duck Detective: The Secret Salami.

Savy Des-Etages as Diana Osterhagen

Savy is an experienced voice actor and audiobook narrator hailing from Lancashire, UK. In the world of video games, Savy has lent her talents to widely popular titles such as Viewfinder, Cassette Beasts, Fallout: London and more!

Antonio Greco as Donny Donato, Casino Enforcer 

Antonio is a versatile voice actor who specialises in character, animation / cartoon, and video game character voices.

Darius T Jackson as Raymond, Sonny, Victor

Darius is a Chicago based voice actor for video games and animations, known for their role as Felix in Cassette Beasts.

Jacob Janerka as Brother Jared

Once described as Australia's ‘most enigmatic’ game developer, Jacob Janerka is known as the creator of the surreal adventure game Paradigm and the upcoming The Dungeon Experience. 

Dave Jones as Lex Lamont, Isaac, Harold

Dave has previously voiced characters in video games such as The Excavation of Hob's Barrow and Planet Zoo, but he is perhaps best known for his role as Halsin in Baldur’s Gate III. This performance earned him a spot on the BAFTA Game Awards longlist for- Best Performance in a Supporting Role.

Amina Koroma as Justice Bailey, Edna, Doris

Based in South London, Amina is co-founder of the British VO Network and a talented voice over artist who reads across Commercials, Drama, Animation and Gaming. In the field of video games, Amina is known for their roles in Baldur’s Gate III and Read Only Memories: Neurodiver.

Nickeem Latty-Morgan as Emmanuel, Sonny

Nickeem is a voice actor and freelance video editor based in South London, specialising in character performances for video games and animation.

notes.content:
Hello there! It's time for the last Loco Motive blog of the year, so let's get straight to it!

As I write this blog post, we’re winding down development here and preparing to spend some well earned time with our family over the Christmas holidays. It’s a time of reflection, so let’s look at all we’ve achieved, and what’s left to come for us in the new year!

🧭2023 Recap🧭

2023! It’s been a year of highlights, but let’s look at some of our biggest milestones:


 We demoed at PAX East and EGX 2023 - the UK's biggest gaming exhibition!
 The game became ‘fully playable’ from start to finish
 Loco Motive was nominated for a Critics’ Choice Award
 We were officially selected to be part of LudoNarracon 2023
 We debuted our first playable demo on Steam as part of Steam Mystery Fest
 Full controller support was added to the game!
 We reached over 70,000+ Wishlists!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/1c3aa8ebdab3448bfdc5c727fa66d54a2ae1a338.jpg

🎤 Voice Acting has begun!🎤 

Many of the questions we’ve received so far have revolved around voice, and if / when Loco Motive will feature voice acting.

I am pleased to confirm that we've recently begun recording dialogue with a professional voice cast, who we couldn’t be more excited about! These talented voice actors have featured in games such as The Legend Of Zelda: Tears Of The Kingdom, Viewfinder, Genshin Impact, Baldur’s Gate III, Starfield and more!

We’ll be announcing the full cast as we record more dialogue and get closer to launch, so keep your eyes peeled for a future announcement. Until then, we'll be keeping you guessing!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/cb2424a1d3614dd48ebe008d9d3589ede18c5c23.png

 ⏪ Subtitle Speed Settings

  🗚  Bigger Text Size Settings

notes.title: Development Update #5
notes.content:
Hello and happy winter! We hope you and your loved ones are staying warm and enjoying the season.

We're excited to report that development is going well, with us recently reaching a significant milestone in the project! We’ll have more to share on that in the new year, so let’s do a little post mortem!

It's been a little over a month since we showcased Loco Motive at AdventureX in London. This was the first time we exhibited the game, and we wanted to share our experience, describe what went well, and look at what could be improved upon.

First, we want to thank everyone who attended the event and provided feedback on our game. We're taking your comments and suggestions to heart!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/d45376c22602e6c2f0bd58c7ff02ce6b07dc13e9.png

During AdventureX, we confirmed that the UK narrative game community is full of supportive and welcoming people. As newcomers to the scene, it was clear that everyone wanted each other to succeed. 
We met many developers and industry veterans who came to the booth and shared their thoughts, ideas and advice with us.

We’re happy to share that people are very excited for Loco Motive! There were often lines of people waiting to play the game during the event, and many attendees came by afterwards to tell us how much they enjoyed it.

Overall, we had a great response and generated a lot of positive buzz. We believe this was due to the game being well-received at the event, word-of-mouth recommendations from other attendees and the fact that we didn't yet have a demo available elsewhere. We're grateful for all the support and feedback we received from those attending!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/a6e6856640225329664b97203f5afe1b567c50ba.png

One area we could improve on in future is the length of the demo. In order to streamline the build, we disabled several puzzle chains in Arthur Ackerman's first act and focused on one overarching puzzle. 

We believed players would get through the demo in around 25-30 minutes, but we noticed they were often spending over an hour in it. This suggests that we could have streamlined things further while still providing a good representation of the game.

In the future, we will likely create a shorter demo. This will help us better manage players' time and provide a more focused experience. Deciding where to end the demo was a challenge for us, but we're confident that we can find a good balance in future iterations.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/3564bc31387cc83a45d6c2db4e0f61883c8bd617.png

We look forward to sharing more updates with you in the coming weeks. In the meantime, we hope you have a wonderful holiday season and a happy new year.

Thank you for your support. We can't wait to share Loco Motive with you!

You can follow us for updates on Twitter or join the official Robust Games Discord.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/db0ed48567ef57238e8659975968b55de889a29d.png

The Music Of Loco Motive

Our composer, Paul Zimmermann is here to talk about his approach to the music of Loco Motive, and the adaptive system we’ve built around the game as you move between carriages:

"My goal with every project is to find a sound that feels authentic to the game and its characters. 
The soundtrack for Loco Motive is turning out to be this fun blend of different styles and periods in music, from big-band swing to 60s spy music and the occasional French-inspired waltz. 

We have quite the varied cast of characters, so it felt natural to try and reflect that in the music."

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/e1d36c7a6f07fcce2b498792255773d2f59aa4bd.jpg

"From a technical standpoint it was important for us to implement the music into the game in a way that it reacts to the gameplay and locations, opposed to having static looping tracks. 

As players roam around the train trying to solve puzzles, the music follows along and changes seamlessly between carriages and characters."

In order to achieve this, I’m writing and then exporting the music in small chunks that allow for fast transitions, meaning, a certain melody-note might be carried over into the next location, or a groove transitions smoothly. Our thinking here is that if players don’t notice it, then we’ve actually achieved what we set out to do!"

notes.title: UI Deep Dive, Discord & Character Spotlight
notes.content:
Hey everyone! Adam from Robust Games here, excited to be bringing you another Loco Motive development blog! 

We promised a deep dive into the UI/UX of the game in our last blog, so award-winning UI Designer Edd Coates was kind enough to volunteer some time to run through his process.

UI Deep Dive

Hi everyone! My name’s Edd Coates and I’m the UI/UX Designer on Loco Motive!  

I wanted to talk a little about my design process, as well as give you a small peek at what you can expect to see when the game launches this year.

Growing up with games such as Monkey Island, Sam & Max and The Dig, I've always been a massive fan of point and click games, which is why I was so excited to be working on Loco Motive.

I had three goals:


 Make the interface feel like an extension of the world and its characters.
 The game should feel as comfortable with a gamepad as it would with a mouse.
 Provide an intuitive gameplay experience that will feel both familiar to fans of the genre, while welcoming to new ones.


First of all, the interface was wireframed in greyscale.  This was to ensure that the contrast and usability was spot on before adding colour and texture.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/5dd59dc2fd00c41910ae14faa1302503e550bc78.gif

Art Deco patterns were sprinkled throughout the menus as a reference to the game’s 1930s setting. I was able to get really creative with these, some early designs even incorporated elements from the train such as the spokes!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/7a6d6c52465599240c048c94f74327a9c560aef6.png

We decided to go with a clean, vector-based art style for the UI (rather than pixel art) to give it some modern flair and ensure that it stands out from the rest of the game.

Traditional verb bars are replaced with a single context button and an inventory menu that can be recalled as needed. This streamlined user experience has you focused less on the nitty-gritty of navigating menus, and more on enjoying the world of Loco Motive.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/d5b10a5f35b45120cde7e681934c4f73a557bf99.gif

We had relatively few challenges on the UX side, with many examples of well-refined Point and Click games to draw inspiration from.  

We looked to titles such as Broken Age and Sam & Max Save The World as they had already solved many of the problems associated with making a point-and-click title playable with a gamepad.

This is just a small taste of what to expect from the interface of Loco Motive!  I’m looking forward to you all seeing the UI in action when the game launches later this year.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/b7de962881344cf0c15da582ce76123d30c2c93d.gif

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/32e92bfb8d5e5bc7edac733bb09e4e974a1f2141.gif

Character Spotlight - Herman Merman

It’s time for our second character spotlight! Next up is the self-declared detective extraordinaire, Herman Merman! 

Herman Merman is a crime novelist who dreams of solving real cases. Always one to project himself as an infamous detective, he's never actually had a real case. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/155e7a7bdfdd0398bd5e3451d22d0f208888aaef.png

Herman’s latest novel is not going down so well with the publishing house, and with waning sales and a new star on the horizon - Herman needs to up his game!

When he receives an unexpected call from Lady Unterwald seeking his employment aboard the Reuss Express, Herman jumps at the opportunity to hone his skills in the field. 

Ever the optimist, even when his employer meets her untimely end - Herman believes he's destined to solve this case. 

There's just one problem, however. He hasn't got a clue!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/c44b474eb0374760d8d4e5927736310fc7789f0c.png

That’s all for now! We’ll be sharing more progress as we go, but in the meantime you can follow us for updates on Twitter or join the community in our brand new Discord channel.

Come aboard and say hello!

notes.title: Introducing Loco Motive!
notes.content:

To add a little steam to our engine, we’ve collaborated with Chucklefish to help publish Loco Motive, and aim to release in Summer 2022 on PC and Nintendo Switch. 

Here's the trailer we just dropped as part of Nintendo's Indie World Showcase - check it out:
[previewyoutube=EFahJJOdMzI;full][/previewyoutube]
Whassit about?
Set aboard a lavish 1930’s express train, Loco Motive follows three larger-than-life characters: a trusty lawyer⚖, an amateur detective🕵🏽‍♂️ and a suave super secret agent🍸, as they gather clues to solve the ominous murder of Lady Unterwald and prove their innocence.

Features

 Inspired by comedy point-and-click adventures of the past
 Solve item-based puzzles, that are satisfying without being frustrating
 Meet a cast of intriguing and suspicious characters, all fully voiced!
 Choose from two control options - take direct character control, or opt for a classic point and click experience
 Beautifully detailed pixel art animation
 Need a little nudge in the right direction? Telephone for assistance with an in-game hint call-line!
 With music from composer Paul Zimmerman (Space Haven, Cave Blazers)

How can I find out more?
Give us a follow on Twitter and check out our website for the latest information on Loco Motive development. You should also check out Chucklefish on Twitter, they’re pretty cool. We’d also appreciate it if you could wishlist Loco Motive, it really helps us!
